name: Manual

accentElements.note: A frame may hold code and its run (the block map's pane stack). A code block is one accent element: its lit line and its teal literal values are its signature (codeBlock), and they stay teal. A terminal's result line is the second.

reference: Stripe's documentation and IBM Plex editorial pages: prose beside code, line numbers, one highlight colour.
pattern: Warm white page, near-black text, one muted teal for the highlighted line.
personality: A patient teacher. Code on one side, the explanation on the other, one line lit at a time.

motion.character: Calm and readable: code types at a human rate, the highlight sweeps 300 ms, the view scrolls, never zooms.
motion.transitions: A scroll to the next block, or a cut.

grammar: Code is real and shown at a readable size, with line numbers.
One highlighted line at a time.
Prose sits beside or under the code, never over it.
Syntax colour uses four hues or fewer.
needs: Real code or a real API to show.

pictures.note: Screenshots of real output only, ungraded, in a window beside the code.

footage.note: No footage: code and prose carry it.

hits.note: A soft key tick when code types in, and only then.

compose.how: The page is code and its run. The question at the text-safe top, the code straight under it, and the run under the code in a pane with the same edges (terminal, `resultRole: "headline"`, `end: "result"`), so the panes fill the page to the text-safe foot. Size each from its rows (B.measure). Under the low band's top at 9:16 the code column is narrower: keep lines short enough that none wraps. A longer run, or a drawing of the result, goes in the next view.

hook.how: The question in prose and the first line of real code, both readable on frame 0. The code types on from there.

moves.move: One lit line: the highlight band in the accent, with the line number in the accent too. It moves in one stride, never sweeps through other lines.

measurable.how: The accent covers a band one row high in the code column while a line is lit.

moves.move: Code types at a human rate (codeBlock `enter: "type"`), with soft key ticks from `typing`, which keeps the ticks to the effects limit.

measurable.how: The ticks stand 6 dB or more over the bed.

moves.move: The view scrolls to the next block; it never zooms.
The output proves the idea: the run prints, and the picture shows what it printed.

props.highlight: one line at a time, on the beat
props.band: "tint" (the default here: the teal band, gutter bar and number)
props.enter: "type" (the first row rests on frame 0 when at is 0, then the rest types on); each highlight after its row is typed (the line anchor's data.typedAt)

blocks.for: Real code at a readable size with line numbers.

props.session: the command and its real output
props.result: true on the one line the run proves
props.resultRole: "headline" when the result is the reveal

blocks.for: The run that proves the code. terminalHeight() gives the panel height for its rows.

props.role: "headline" for the question of the hook (the hook's role); "body" for prose beside the code

blocks.for: Prose beside or above the code, never over it.
The scroll to the next block.

props.title: the file or the shell
props.inset: the default, shared by every pane

blocks.for: One window for code and output, so their edges align (paneStack).

avoid.why: Manual reads at a human pace.
Pictures are rare here; the code and its output are the subject.

ends.how: A last run with a larger input: the output prints, and the cursor blinks on the last line.
ends.with: the last command prints its result (`result: true`) on the last bar; the cursor blinks to the end

mix.note: Mellow and unhurried. A key tick under typed code, and only then.

shots.match: One program: the code, the run and the output are about the same function.

subjectsToAvoid: Fibonacci numbers or the golden spiral
FizzBuzz or a sort of ten numbers
